prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1386; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the claimant reported being rear-ended while stopped at a traffic light. The claimant is not represented by counsel, and I explained the claims process and what documents will be needed.

Entry 2: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the vehicles made contact in the manner the claimant described. Photos taken at the scene are consistent with that account, and two independent witnesses gave matching statements.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The damage to the rear of the claimant's car appears largely in line with the impact described, and I found no record of earlier damage to the vehicle.

Entry 4: Confirmed with the policyholder's records that the driver involved is a member of the household and is covered under the policy. The loss date falls within the active coverage period, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 5: Claimant reports a knee injury from the impact. The reported injury is plausible for a rear-end collision of this kind, and the claimant has no known prior injury to that area.

Entry 6: Treatment has followed a typical course, with visits tapering as the claimant's knee improved. The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far.

Entry 7: Reviewed the treatment records and medical bills against the expected recovery timeline. The care provided is reasonable for the injury reported, and no further action is needed beyond routine closure documentation.
